Roadmap alignment and pilot next steps

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Rao (Redwood AE), Jules Park (Redwood CSM), Marta Ivanov (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Argus Head of ML), Marcus Chen (Argus Platform Eng), Priya Shah (Argus CTO)

Summary: quarterly business review / health check. Covering usage, costs, reliability incidents, roadmap, and next steps.

00:00 Lena Ortiz: okay everyone thanks for coming, I think we have about 45 minutes so we'll start, yes this is Lena from Argus, thanks Samir and team for joining.
00:12 Samir Rao: hey Lena, great to see you, Jules and Marta from our side, hi Priya, Marcus, thanks for squeezing us in.
00:20 Marcus Chen: no problem, we got the calendar, excited to go through the numbers.
00:35 Jules Park: quick agenda—usage/cost trends, reliability incidents, discussion on Dedicated pilot and security questions, and wrap with action items.
00:50 Priya Shah: sounds good.
01:10 Samir Rao: quick high level—usage is up ~28% qtr-over-qtr, tokens per month up driven by our routing and a new customer-facing summarization route. We flagged top 3 routes that account for ~65% of spend.
01:40 Lena Ortiz: yes that's the summarization route, prompt length is long, lots of context—we suspect KV cache hits are low because requests don't share prefixes.
02:05 Marta Ivanov: that would explain cost; two quick levers we recommended before: prefix caching for repeated contexts and batching for shorter assistant flows. Also quantization on the Llama-variant we're using gave 15-20% token cost reduction in similar workloads.
02:40 Marcus Chen: curious about latency tradeoff with quantization—our SLO is 250ms p50 and 800ms p95 for the customer edges. We saw some p95 spikes early October.
03:05 Marta Ivanov: correct, quantization can slightly impact p95 depending on kernel choices, but our optimizer recommends per-route profiles; for high percentile SLOs we can pin to higher-precision variants and still use quantized workers for batch offline tasks.
03:40 Priya Shah: can you walk us through the October incident—the latency spike?
04:00 Jules Park: yes so on Oct 11 we saw a tail latency spike to ~1.8s p95 for one region tied to a hot-shard during an autoscale flapping event. Root cause was a mis-sized pre-warm threshold and a race in the routing fallback which retried to a slower variant. We've implemented a fix for pre-warm thresholds and added circuit-breaker style fallback delays.
04:45 Lena Ortiz: ok that matches what we saw in our logs. Did Redwood add any tracing to capture KV cache misses?
05:00 Marta Ivanov: we added additional tracing hooks and will surface token-level breakdown in the console per route; you should see prefix/KV cache hit rates in the next console update (ETA: 24–48 hours).
05:30 Marcus Chen: on Dedicated—we're interested in reserved capacity for predictable costs but worried about utilization. How does Redwood handle autoscaling and burst to hosted?
06:00 Samir Rao: good question—Dedicated offers a reserved GPU pool with configurable autoscaling policies and a burst-to-hosted option for overflow. You can set a hard cap to prevent burst if you need strict isolation. Pricing mixes a base reserved fee plus usage for burst. We'll include a model for your current traffic patterns in the pricing sheet.
06:35 Lena Ortiz: what's the SLA for Dedicated?
06:45 Samir Rao: Dedicated has an SLA target for uptime and latency tiers depending on committed tier; we'll include the SLA language in the docs we send.
07:05 Priya Shah: security—SOC 2, SSO, KMS integration. We need to know about key management and audit logs for our compliance team.
07:30 Jules Park: Redwood supports KMS integrations (AWS/GCP/Azure) for envelope encryption, and we can provide audit logs and per-request traceability. For SSO we support SAML/Okta and RBAC roles. We'll upload SOC 2 attestation and the KMS integration guide after the call.
08:00 Marcus Chen: any issues with data residency? We have EU customers and may need region controls.
08:12 Marta Ivanov: yes regional routing is supported, you can pin models and routes to regions; for Private deployments we offer VPC and on-prem options if required.
08:35 Lena Ortiz: given our peaks are predictable, we'd like to try a 4-week Dedicated pilot to measure tail latency and cost delta. What's the usual turnaround?
08:52 Samir Rao: we can stand up a pilot in 7–10 business days once we have account creds and a baseline workload. Marta will coordinate the perf run with you.
09:10 Marta Ivanov: for the perf run I want sample traces, top prompts, and a small synthetic load plan to replay at p95/p99 traffic—can we get those?
09:25 Lena Ortiz: yes we can export traces, Marcus will share.
09:35 Marcus Chen: I'll drop a redacted trace and top prompt templates into the shared folder by Wednesday.
09:45 Priya Shah: about pricing—we need a clear estimate including Dedicated reserved fees and expected unit costs with and without quantization.
10:05 Samir Rao: will send a pricing sheet with Dedicated pilot estimate and a couple scenarios: current hosted, Dedicated with 50% utilization, Dedicated with burst-to-hosted.
10:25 Lena Ortiz: great. Also want to check rollback/fallback if Dedicated misses SLOs—can Redwood fallback to other variants automatically?
10:40 Marta Ivanov: yes there are routing policies—automated fallback to compatible model variants or to hosted capacity, with A/B or canary rollouts and automatic fallback rules. We'll share an example policy.
11:05 Marcus Chen: one more on observability—we'd like token-level cost per route and per-user breakdown for chargeback. Is that available now?
11:25 Jules Park: token-level breakdown per route is available in the console; per-user breakdown depends on your event tagging but we can configure a route-level tag to flow through billing.
11:45 Priya Shah: any blockers on our side for the pilot?
12:00 Lena Ortiz: mostly internal approvals, but technical wise we can provide vault keys and a VPC peering request if needed.
12:15 Marta Ivanov: for the initial pilot we'll recommend using Dedicated with an isolated subnet and KMS integration—no peering required for the first run, we'll use secure transit. If you want VPC peering for longer pilots we can set that up.
12:40 Samir Rao: recap—Redwood to send pricing and SOC2/KMS docs, Marta to schedule perf benchmark, Argus to send traces and prompts.
13:00 Priya Shah: thanks all, that works.
13:10 Samir Rao: thanks everyone we'll follow up on the thread and lock in dates.
13:20 Meeting end.
